title: Part
spec: Create a new coordinate system with the Euler angles set to zero degrees and the translation vector also set to zero. On the first face, draw a two-dimensional sketch consisting of a single loop. The loop includes four lines: the first line starts at the origin (0.0, 0.0) and ends at (0.75, 0.0); the second line starts at (0.75, 0.0) and ends at (0.75, 0.0313); the third line starts at (0.75, 0.0313) and ends at (0.0, 0.0313); and the fourth line completes the loop by starting at (0.0, 0.0313) and ending at the origin (0.0, 0.0). Scale the two-dimensional sketch by a factor of 0.75. Transform the scaled sketch into three dimensions by rotating it using the Euler angles [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] and translating it using the translation vector [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]. Extrude the sketch 0.0156 units along the normal direction to create a new solid body. This results in a cylindrical object with a rectangular section at one end, measuring 0.7500000000000001 units in length, 0.03125000000000001 units in width, and 0.015625000000000003 units in height.

# Extrude the sketch

# Assign the final model to 'r'

lanes.label: Cadabra 4B (ours) · best of 8
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0313, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0313, 0.0156) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0156) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90, 0, -90) and the translation vector is (0, 0, 0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0313) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0313) \

import cadquery as cq

# Main body: long rectangular bar
# X = 0.7500 (length), Y = 0.0313 (width), Z = 0.0156 (thickness)
r = cq.Workplane("XY").box(0.7500, 0.0313, 0.0156)

# Small chamfers visible on the end faces (seen in FRONT and ISOMETRIC views)
r = r.faces(">X or <X").edges().chamfer(0.002)
